purpose: V2-P02 §17 — live snapshot MG0 parity would compare Path A (live OpenMetadataProvider → MG0) vs Path B (canonical-snapshot-backed Static provider → MG0) using the SAME canonical bytes. NOT_EXERCISED because no live server is reachable.

deterministic_parity_evidence_still_hold.note: V2-P01R already proved that Static and OpenMetadata providers produce byte-equivalent MG0 output when fed logically equivalent canonical metadata through the actual MG0 pipeline.
invariants_verified_deterministically: S0 serialized context text identical byte-for-byte
deterministic_parity_evidence_still_hold.why_this_is_necessary_but_not_sufficient: Provider parity on synthetic canonical fixtures proves the mapping+transport layer is correct FOR THAT SHAPE OF INPUT. It does not prove the live server actually returns that shape of input. V2-P02 requires exercising the live path to confirm.

live_snapshot_parity_procedure_when_envi: 2. Serialize the returned CatalogTable[] to a canonical snapshot on disk (excluding provenance timestamps to keep the snapshot stable). Record snapshot sha256.
3. Build a temporary StaticMetadataProvider (or an InMemoryCatalog seeded directly) from that same canonical snapshot.
4. For a bounded generic pilot question, run both providers through the actual MG0 pipeline (as V2-P01R does).
5. Assert equivalence on selected_tables, selected_columns, relationships, retrieval signals, S0 context text — the same six invariants V2-P01R checks.
6. If any invariant fails, the failure must be in provider transport/mapping, not in metadata content (both paths use the same canonical bytes).
